chunks: As for what Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Abū Hāshim al-Jaʿfarī, he said:

I was with Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام on a boat on the Tigris when the time for salat came. So I said: “May I be made your ransom, shall we perform salat in congregation?” He said: “Do not perform salat in congregation in the middle of a valley.”
So the intended meaning in this narration is a form of reprehensibility, or a state of necessity in which one is not able to perform salat in congregation.

key_terms.السَّفِينَةِ: a boat or ship, the setting in which the prayer ruling is discussed
key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: necessity, a constraining circumstance affecting the possibility of congregational salat
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: reprehensibility, indicating that the prohibition may signify dislike rather than absolute forbiddance
key_terms.بَطْنِ وَادٍ: the middle or low part of a valley, mentioned as the place connected to the ruling
key_terms.جَمَاعَةٍ: congregation, meaning prayer performed collectively behind an Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing congregational salat in a boat according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of performing congregational salat in a boat. The apparent prohibition is understood as indicating karahah (reprehensibility) or a circumstance of necessity in which congregational salat cannot properly be established.
